---

> **Research question:** Do weekly changes in Russia-Ukraine conflict intensity (ACLED
> violent events) help explain weekly changes in worldwide Google search interest for the
> term *"ukraine war"*? Sample: 2023-2026, n approx 170 weekly observations. 2022 is excluded
> due to a visible normalisation discontinuity in the stitched Google Trends series.

---

> **How to run:** Clone the repository, open this `.Rmd` file in RStudio (it lives in
> `Scripts/`) and hit **Knit**. No path editing is needed. Raw ACLED data are not
> redistributed (ACLED terms of use); see `Data/ACLED/README.md` to download them.
> VIX and S&P 500 are downloaded automatically from FRED and Yahoo Finance.

---

```{r packages}
# Edit this block to restyle all figures at once.
theme_project <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0,
                                       margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey35", hjust = 0,

      axis.title        = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey20", face = "bold"),
      axis.text         = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey30"),
      axis.line         = element_line(color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4),

      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
    )
}

# BOOTSTRAP CI
# Computes residual-bootstrap confidence bands for any ADL/lm IRF.

bootstrap_irf_ci <- function(model, own_lag_names, conflict_lag_names,
                              h = 20, n_boot = 500, ci_level = 0.90) {
  Y      <- model$model[, 1]
  X      <- model.matrix(model)
  resids <- residuals(model)
  coefs  <- coef(model)
  n      <- length(Y)

  # Helper: compute one IRF from a coefficient vector
  compute_one_irf <- function(b) {
    phi   <- as.numeric(b[own_lag_names]);       phi[is.na(phi)]   <- 0
    theta <- as.numeric(b[conflict_lag_names]);  theta[is.na(theta)] <- 0
    irf   <- numeric(h)
    for (t in 1:h) {
      direct     <- if (t <= length(theta)) theta[t] else 0
      propagated <- if (t > 1)
        sum(phi[1:min(t-1,length(phi))] * irf[(t-1):max(1,t-length(phi))]) else 0
      irf[t] <- direct + propagated
    }
    irf
  }

  # Point estimate
  irf_point <- compute_one_irf(coefs)

  # Bootstrap loop: resample residuals, reconstruct Y, refit, recompute IRF
  boot_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_boot, ncol = h)
  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    Y_boot        <- X %*% coefs + sample(resids, n, replace = TRUE)
    df_boot       <- as.data.frame(cbind(Y_boot, X[, -1]))
    names(df_boot)[1] <- names(model$model)[1]
    fit_boot      <- tryCatch(lm(reformulate(names(df_boot)[-1], names(df_boot)[1]),
                                 data = df_boot),
                              error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(fit_boot))
      boot_mat[b, ] <- compute_one_irf(coef(fit_boot))
  }

  alpha <- (1 - ci_level) / 2
  list(
    point = irf_point,
    lower = apply(boot_mat, 2, quantile, probs = alpha,     na.rm = TRUE),
    upper = apply(boot_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 1 - alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}
```

## ACLED conflict data

```{r load-acled}
acled_file <- list.files(here("Data/ACLED"), pattern = "^Europe-Central-Asia.*\\.csv$",
                         full.names = TRUE)[1]
if (is.na(acled_file)) stop("ACLED file not found: see Data/ACLED/README.md")
acled_data <- read.csv(acled_file)
```

```{r build-conflict}
ukraine_acled <- subset(acled_data, COUNTRY == "Ukraine")
ukraine_acled_narrow <- subset(ukraine_acled,
  EVENT_TYPE %in% c("Battles","Explosions/Remote violence","Violence against civilians"))
weekly_ukraine <- aggregate(EVENTS ~ WEEK, data = ukraine_acled_narrow, sum)
weekly_ukraine$week_date <- as.Date(weekly_ukraine$WEEK, format = "%d-%B-%Y")
weekly_ukraine <- weekly_ukraine[order(weekly_ukraine$week_date), ]
weekly_ukraine <- subset(weekly_ukraine, week_date >= as.Date("2022-01-01"))

russia_acled <- subset(acled_data, COUNTRY == "Russia")
russia_acled_narrow <- subset(russia_acled,
  EVENT_TYPE %in% c("Battles","Explosions/Remote violence","Violence against civilians"))
weekly_russia <- aggregate(EVENTS ~ WEEK, data = russia_acled_narrow, sum)
weekly_russia$week_date <- as.Date(weekly_russia$WEEK, format = "%d-%B-%Y")
weekly_russia <- weekly_russia[order(weekly_russia$week_date), ]
weekly_russia <- subset(weekly_russia, week_date >= as.Date("2022-01-01"))

ukraine_w <- weekly_ukraine[, c("week_date","EVENTS")]; names(ukraine_w)[2] <- "ukraine_events"
russia_w  <- weekly_russia[,  c("week_date","EVENTS")]; names(russia_w)[2]  <- "russia_events"

combined_weekly <- merge(ukraine_w, russia_w, by = "week_date", all = TRUE)
combined_weekly$ukraine_events[is.na(combined_weekly$ukraine_events)] <- 0
combined_weekly$russia_events[is.na(combined_weekly$russia_events)]   <- 0
combined_weekly$combined_events <- combined_weekly$ukraine_events + combined_weekly$russia_events
combined_weekly <- combined_weekly[order(combined_weekly$week_date), ]
acled_2023 <- subset(combined_weekly, week_date >= as.Date("2023-01-01"))
```

## Google Trends data (worldwide)

```{r load-google}
gt_2023 <- read.csv(here("Data/Google Trends/Worldwide/2023.csv"))
gt_2024 <- read.csv(here("Data/Google Trends/Worldwide/2024.csv"))
gt_2025 <- read.csv(here("Data/Google Trends/Worldwide/2025.csv"))
gt_2026 <- read.csv(here("Data/Google Trends/Worldwide/2026.csv"))

for (df_name in c("gt_2023","gt_2024","gt_2025","gt_2026")) {
  tmp <- get(df_name)
  tmp$Time        <- as.Date(tmp$Time)
  tmp$ukraine.war <- as.numeric(tmp$ukraine.war)
  assign(df_name, tmp)
}
google_weekly <- rbind(gt_2023, gt_2024, gt_2025, gt_2026)
google_weekly <- google_weekly[order(google_weekly$Time), ]
```

## Merge ACLED and Google Trends

```{r merge}
google_weekly$Time_aligned <- google_weekly$Time + 6
project_data_2023on <- merge(acled_2023, google_weekly,
                             by.x = "week_date", by.y = "Time_aligned", all = FALSE)
project_data_2023on <- project_data_2023on[order(project_data_2023on$week_date), ]
cat("Merged dataset:", nrow(project_data_2023on), "weekly observations\n")
cat("Date range:    ", format(min(project_data_2023on$week_date)), "to",
    format(max(project_data_2023on$week_date)), "\n")
```

## Raw data plots

```{r plot-raw, fig.height=7}
p1 <- ggplot(project_data_2023on, aes(x = week_date, y = combined_events)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1A5276", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(project_data_2023on$combined_events),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#C0392B", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "ACLED: Weekly Conflict Intensity",
       subtitle = "2023 onward — combined Ukraine + Russia violent events (dashed = mean)",
       x = NULL, y = "Violent events per week") +
  theme_project()

p2 <- ggplot(project_data_2023on, aes(x = week_date, y = ukraine.war)) +
  geom_line(color = "#C0392B", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(project_data_2023on$ukraine.war, na.rm = TRUE),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#1A5276", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Google Trends: 'ukraine war' Worldwide",
       subtitle = "2023 onward — weekly search interest index (0-100, dashed = mean)",
       x = "Week", y = "Google Trends index") +
  theme_project()

p1 / p2
```

> **Visual takeaway:** Conflict intensity is persistent and upward-trending — first
> signal of non-stationarity. Google Trends is spiky and burst-driven.

# Stationarity Analysis

## Formal tests in levels

```{r stationarity-levels}
adf_conflict  <- adf.test(project_data_2023on$combined_events, k = 5)
adf_google    <- adf.test(na.omit(project_data_2023on$ukraine.war), k = 5)
kpss_conflict <- kpss.test(project_data_2023on$combined_events, null = "Level")
kpss_google   <- kpss.test(na.omit(project_data_2023on$ukraine.war), null = "Level")

cat("=== ADF (levels) ===\n")
cat("Conflict: p =", round(adf_conflict$p.value, 3), "\n")
cat("Google:   p =", round(adf_google$p.value,   3), "\n\n")
cat("=== KPSS (levels) ===\n")
cat("Conflict: p =", round(kpss_conflict$p.value, 3), "\n")
cat("Google:   p =", round(kpss_google$p.value,   3), "\n")
```

> Conflict is clearly non-stationary. **Decision: first-difference both series.**

## First differences and standardisation

```{r first-differences}
# Step 1: first differences
project_data_2023on$d_conflict <- c(NA, diff(project_data_2023on$combined_events))
project_data_2023on$d_google   <- c(NA, diff(project_data_2023on$ukraine.war))
project_data_2023on$d_ukraine  <- c(NA, diff(project_data_2023on$ukraine_events))
project_data_2023on$d_russia   <- c(NA, diff(project_data_2023on$russia_events))

# Step 2: z-score standardisation
# Puts conflict (0-2000 events) and Google Trends (0-100 index) on the same scale.
# Coefficients now read as SDs. p-values and significance are unchanged.
project_data_2023on$d_conflict <- as.numeric(scale(project_data_2023on$d_conflict))
project_data_2023on$d_google   <- as.numeric(scale(project_data_2023on$d_google))
project_data_2023on$d_ukraine  <- as.numeric(scale(project_data_2023on$d_ukraine))
project_data_2023on$d_russia   <- as.numeric(scale(project_data_2023on$d_russia))

# Step 3: clean vectors for ACF/PACF/periodogram
d_conflict_clean <- na.omit(project_data_2023on$d_conflict)
d_google_clean   <- na.omit(project_data_2023on$d_google)

cat("=== ADF (first differences, standardised) ===\n")
cat("d_conflict: p =", round(adf.test(d_conflict_clean, k=5)$p.value, 3), "\n")
cat("d_google:   p =", round(adf.test(d_google_clean,   k=5)$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
cat("=== KPSS (first differences, standardised) ===\n")
cat("d_conflict: p =", round(kpss.test(d_conflict_clean)$p.value, 3), "\n")
cat("d_google:   p =", round(kpss.test(d_google_clean)$p.value,   3), "\n")
```

```{r plot-differences, fig.height=7}
p3 <- ggplot(project_data_2023on, aes(x = week_date, y = d_conflict)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1A5276", linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#C0392B", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "First Difference — Conflict Intensity (Standardised)",
       x = NULL, y = "SD units") +
  theme_project()

p4 <- ggplot(project_data_2023on, aes(x = week_date, y = d_google)) +
  geom_line(color = "#C0392B", linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#1A5276", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "First Difference — Google Trends (Standardised)",
       x = "Week", y = "SD units") +
  theme_project()

p3 / p4
```

```{r seasonality-ftest}
season_data <- na.omit(data.frame(
  d_google   = project_data_2023on$d_google,
  d_conflict = project_data_2023on$d_conflict,
  month      = as.factor(project_data_2023on$month)
))

ftest_c <- anova(lm(d_conflict ~ 1, data = season_data), lm(d_conflict ~ month, data = season_data))
cat("Seasonal F-test — d_google:   p =", round(ftest_g[2, "Pr(>F)"], 3), "\n")
cat("Seasonal F-test — d_conflict: p =", round(ftest_c[2, "Pr(>F)"], 3), "\n")
```

> No seasonal pattern. **No seasonal adjustment needed.**

# ADL Model Selection

```{r create-lags}
max_lags <- 3
CONFLICT   <- project_data_2023on$d_conflict
names_lags <- "lag0"
for (i in 1:max_lags) {
  CONFLICT   <- cbind(CONFLICT,
                      c(rep(NA,i), project_data_2023on$d_conflict[1:(nrow(project_data_2023on)-i)]))
  names_lags <- c(names_lags, paste0("lag",i))
}
colnames(CONFLICT) <- names_lags
d_google_lag1 <- c(NA, project_data_2023on$d_google[1:(nrow(project_data_2023on)-1)])
model_data <- na.omit(data.frame(d_google = project_data_2023on$d_google,
                                 d_google_lag1 = d_google_lag1, CONFLICT))
cat("Observations available:", nrow(model_data), "\n")
```

```{r estimate-models}
m1 <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1,                             data = model_data)
m2 <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + lag0,                      data = model_data)
m3 <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + lag0 + lag1,               data = model_data)
m4 <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + lag0 + lag1 + lag2,        data = model_data)
m5 <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + lag0 + lag1 + lag2 + lag3, data = model_data)
```

```{r aic-bic}
model_list      <- list(m1, m2, m3, m4, m5)
model_names_sel <- c("m1: own lag only","m2: +lag0","m3: +lag0-1","m4: +lag0-2","m5: +lag0-3")
ic_table <- data.frame(
  Model = model_names_sel,
  k     = sapply(model_list, function(m) length(coef(m))),
  AIC   = round(sapply(model_list, AIC), 2),
  BIC   = round(sapply(model_list, BIC), 2)
)
print(ic_table)
cat("\nBest by AIC:", model_names_sel[which.min(ic_table$AIC)], "\n")
cat("Best by BIC:", model_names_sel[which.min(ic_table$BIC)], "\n")
```

> **AIC selects m4; BIC selects m1.** We adopt m4 and augment next.

---

# Preferred Model: m4b

```{r augmented-model}
model_data$d_google_lag2 <- c(NA, model_data$d_google_lag1[1:(nrow(model_data)-1)])
m4b <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + d_google_lag2 + lag0 + lag1 + lag2, data = model_data)
summary(m4b)
```

```{r residual-diagnostics-m4b, fig.height=7}
res_m4b <- residuals(m4b)
par(mfrow = c(3,1), mar = c(4,4.5,3,1), bg = "white")
plot(res_m4b, type = "l", col = "#1A5276", lwd = 2,
     main = "Residuals — m4b", xlab = "Week", ylab = "Residual",
     cex.main = 1.2, cex.axis = 1.1, cex.lab = 1.2)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey50", lwd = 1.2)
acf(res_m4b,  lag.max = 22, main = "ACF of Residuals — m4b",
    col = "#1A5276", lwd = 2, cex.main = 1.2, cex.axis = 1.1)
pacf(res_m4b, lag.max = 22, main = "PACF of Residuals — m4b",
     col = "#1A5276", lwd = 2, cex.main = 1.2, cex.axis = 1.1)
par(mfrow = c(1,1))

bg_m4  <- bgtest(m4,  order = 4)
bg_m4b <- bgtest(m4b, order = 4)
cat("Breusch-Godfrey — m4:  p =", round(bg_m4$p.value,  3), "\n")
cat("Breusch-Godfrey — m4b: p =", round(bg_m4b$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
cat("m4  — AIC:", round(AIC(m4),  2), "| BIC:", round(BIC(m4),  2), "\n")
cat("m4b — AIC:", round(AIC(m4b), 2), "| BIC:", round(BIC(m4b), 2), "\n")
```

```{r hac-m4b}
hac_se_m4b <- sqrt(diag(NeweyWest(m4b, lag = 4, prewhite = FALSE)))
cat("=== m4b: OLS vs HAC ===\n")
stargazer(m4b, m4b, type = "text",
          column.labels = c("OLS","HAC"),
          se = list(NULL, hac_se_m4b),
          keep.stat = "n", no.space = TRUE)
```

# Impulse Response Function (m4b) with Bootstrap Confidence Bands

The shaded band is a **90% bootstrap confidence interval** (500 replications, residual
resampling). If the band excludes zero at a given horizon, the response is statistically
significant there.

```{r irf-m4b, fig.height=5}
set.seed(42)
nb.periods <- 20

phi_m4b  <- c(coef(m4b)["d_google_lag1"], coef(m4b)["d_google_lag2"])
beta_m4b <- c(coef(m4b)["lag0"], coef(m4b)["lag1"], coef(m4b)["lag2"])

IRF_m4b <- sim.arma(c = 0, phi = phi_m4b, theta = beta_m4b, sigma = 1,
                    T = nb.periods, y.0 = rep(0,2), nb.sim = 1, make.IRF = 1)

ci_m4b <- bootstrap_irf_ci(
  m4b,
  own_lag_names      = c("d_google_lag1","d_google_lag2"),
  conflict_lag_names = c("lag0","lag1","lag2"),
  h = nb.periods, n_boot = 500, ci_level = 0.90
)

df_irf_m4b <- data.frame(
  week  = 0:(nb.periods-1),
  irf   = ci_m4b$point,
  lower = ci_m4b$lower,
  upper = ci_m4b$upper
)

cum_effect_m4b <- sum(ci_m4b$point)
df_irf_m4b_plot <- subset(df_irf_m4b, week <= 10)

ggplot(df_irf_m4b_plot, aes(x = week)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#1A5276", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(aes(y = irf), color = "#1A5276", linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(aes(y = irf), color = "#1A5276", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    subtitle = NULL,
    x = "Weeks after shock",
    y = "SD units (search attention)"
  ) +
  theme_project()

cat("Multipliers:\n"); print(round(ci_m4b$point, 4))
cat("Cumulative:", round(cum_effect_m4b, 4), "\n")
```

## Robustness: OLS vs ARMA-X

```{r armax, fig.height=5}
nb.lags.exog <- 2
CONF_X <- model_data$lag0
for (i in 1:nb.lags.exog) CONF_X <- cbind(CONF_X, model_data[[paste0("lag",i)]])
colnames(CONF_X) <- paste0("lag", 0:nb.lags.exog)
good      <- complete.cases(model_data$d_google, CONF_X)
res.armax <- estim.armax(Y = model_data$d_google[good], p = 2, q = 0, X = CONF_X[good,])

IRF_armax <- sim.arma(c = 0, phi = res.armax$phi, theta = res.armax$beta, sigma = 1,
                      T = nb.periods, y.0 = rep(0, length(res.armax$phi)),
                      nb.sim = 1, make.IRF = 1)

df_cmp <- data.frame(
  week   = rep(0:(nb.periods-1), 2),
  irf    = c(ci_m4b$point, IRF_armax),
  method = rep(c("OLS (m4b)","ARMA-X(2,0,2)"), each = nb.periods)
)

ggplot(df_cmp, aes(x = week, y = irf, color = method, linetype = method)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.4) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("OLS (m4b)" = "#1A5276", "ARMA-X(2,0,2)" = "#C0392B")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("OLS (m4b)" = "solid", "ARMA-X(2,0,2)" = "dashed")) +
  labs(title = "IRF Comparison: OLS (m4b) vs ARMA-X(2,0,2)",
       subtitle = paste0("Cumulative OLS: ", round(sum(ci_m4b$point), 3),
                         "  |  Cumulative ARMA-X: ", round(sum(IRF_armax), 3)),
       x = "Weeks after shock", y = "SD units (search attention)") +
  theme_project()
```

> Both IRFs virtually identical -- OLS results robust to estimation method.

# VAR and Granger Causality

```{r var-granger}
var_data <- na.omit(data.frame(d_google   = project_data_2023on$d_google,
                               d_conflict = project_data_2023on$d_conflict))
var_select    <- VARselect(var_data, lag.max = 6)
p_bic         <- var_select$selection["SC(n)"]
estimated_var <- VAR(var_data, p = p_bic)

Phi <- Acoef(estimated_var); PHI <- make.PHI(Phi)
cat("Eigenvalues:", round(abs(eigen(PHI)$values), 4), "\n\n")
cat("H0: d_conflict does NOT Granger-cause d_google\n")
print(grangertest(var_data$d_google, var_data$d_conflict, order = p_bic))
cat("H0: d_google does NOT Granger-cause d_conflict\n")
print(grangertest(var_data$d_conflict, var_data$d_google, order = p_bic))
```

> No reverse causality -- ADL framework validated.

```{r split-conflict-models}
model_data_split <- na.omit(data.frame(

))

  c(NA, model_data_split$d_google_lag1[1:(nrow(model_data_split)-1)])
model_data_split <- na.omit(model_data_split)

mA_split <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + d_google_lag2 + d_ukraine + d_ukraine_lag1 + d_ukraine_lag2,
               data = model_data_split)
mB_split <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + d_google_lag2 + d_russia  + d_russia_lag1  + d_russia_lag2,
               data = model_data_split)
cat("Model A (Ukraine) — AIC:", round(AIC(mA_split),2), "| BIC:", round(BIC(mA_split),2), "\n")
cat("Model B (Russia)  — AIC:", round(AIC(mB_split),2), "| BIC:", round(BIC(mB_split),2), "\n")
```

```{r irf-split, fig.height=5}
set.seed(42)

ci_ukraine <- bootstrap_irf_ci(mA_split,
    own_lag_names      = c("d_google_lag1","d_google_lag2"),

df_irf_split <- data.frame(

)

ggplot(df_irf_split_plot, aes(x = week, color = territory, fill = territory)) +

                                "Russia territory"  = "#C0392B")) +

```

> **Normalisation confirmed.** Russia attacks generate far more attention. Ukraine attacks'

# Extension 1 — Audience Heterogeneity

- **Pro-Ukraine:** Poland, Sweden, United Kingdom, Estonia
- **Pro-Russia:** Serbia, India, Vietnam, Indonesia

```{r load-countries}
path_uk <- paste0(here("Data/Google Trends/Pro Ukraine"), "/")
path_ru <- paste0(here("Data/Google Trends/Pro Russia"),  "/")

load_country <- function(country, path) {
  years <- c(2023, 2024, 2025, 2026)
  df_list <- lapply(years, function(yr) {
    df           <- read.csv(paste0(path, country, "_", yr, ".csv"))
    colnames(df) <- c("Time","index")
    df$index     <- as.numeric(df$index)
    df$Time      <- tryCatch(as.Date(df$Time, format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
                             error = function(e) as.Date(df$Time, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))
    if (all(is.na(df$Time))) df$Time <- as.Date(df$Time, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
    df
  })
  df_all <- do.call(rbind, df_list)
  df_all <- df_all[!duplicated(df_all$Time), ]
  df_all[df_all$Time >= as.Date("2023-01-01"), ]
}

Estonia <- load_country("Estonia",path_uk); Poland    <- load_country("Poland",   path_uk)
Sweden  <- load_country("Sweden", path_uk); UK        <- load_country("UK",       path_uk)
India   <- load_country("India",  path_ru); Indonesia <- load_country("Indonesia",path_ru)
Serbia  <- load_country("Serbia", path_ru); Vietnam   <- load_country("Vietnam",  path_ru)
cat("All countries loaded\n")
```

```{r group-averages}
for (obj in c("Estonia","Poland","Sweden","UK","India","Indonesia","Serbia","Vietnam")) {
  tmp <- get(obj); tmp$Time <- tmp$Time + 6; assign(obj, tmp)
}
pro_ukraine <- data.frame(
  Time_aligned     = Estonia$Time,
  gt_ukraine_group = rowMeans(cbind(Estonia$index,Poland$index,
                                    Sweden$index,UK$index), na.rm=TRUE))
pro_russia <- data.frame(
  Time_aligned    = India$Time,
  gt_russia_group = rowMeans(cbind(India$index,Indonesia$index,
                                   Serbia$index,Vietnam$index), na.rm=TRUE))
```

```{r first-diff-groups, fig.height=6}
d_gt_russia_group  <- as.numeric(scale(diff(pro_russia$gt_russia_group)))

dates_russia_diff  <- pro_russia$Time_aligned[-1]

cat("Pro-Ukraine — ADF p:", round(adf.test(d_gt_ukraine_group)$p.value,3),

df_groups <- data.frame(

              c(length(d_gt_ukraine_group), length(d_gt_russia_group)))
)

ggplot(df_groups, aes(x = week, y = value, color = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
```


```{r build-lag-matrix-ext}
n <- nrow(project_ext)
project_ext$d_google_lag1     <- c(NA, project_ext$d_google[1:(n-1)])
project_ext$d_google_lag2     <- c(NA,NA,project_ext$d_google[1:(n-2)])

project_ext$d_ukraine_lag1    <- c(NA, project_ext$d_ukraine[1:(n-1)])
project_ext$d_ukraine_lag2    <- c(NA,NA,project_ext$d_ukraine[1:(n-2)])
project_ext$d_russia_lag0     <- project_ext$d_russia
project_ext$d_russia_lag1     <- c(NA, project_ext$d_russia[1:(n-1)])
project_ext$d_russia_lag2     <- c(NA,NA,project_ext$d_russia[1:(n-2)])
```

```{r six-models}
mA <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + d_google_lag2 +
           d_ukraine_lag0 + d_ukraine_lag1 + d_ukraine_lag2, data = project_ext)
mB <- lm(d_google ~ d_google_lag1 + d_google_lag2 +
           d_russia_lag0  + d_russia_lag1  + d_russia_lag2,  data = project_ext)
mC <- lm(d_gt_ukraine_group ~ d_gt_ukraine_lag1 + d_gt_ukraine_lag2 +
           d_ukraine_lag0 + d_ukraine_lag1 + d_ukraine_lag2, data = project_ext)
mD <- lm(d_gt_ukraine_group ~ d_gt_ukraine_lag1 + d_gt_ukraine_lag2 +
           d_russia_lag0  + d_russia_lag1  + d_russia_lag2,  data = project_ext)
mE <- lm(d_gt_russia_group ~ d_gt_russia_lag1 + d_gt_russia_lag2 +
           d_ukraine_lag0 + d_ukraine_lag1 + d_ukraine_lag2, data = project_ext)
mF <- lm(d_gt_russia_group ~ d_gt_russia_lag1 + d_gt_russia_lag2 +
           d_russia_lag0  + d_russia_lag1  + d_russia_lag2,  data = project_ext)

models_6      <- list(mA, mB, mC, mD, mE, mF)
model_names_6 <- c("A: World~UKR","B: World~RUS",
                   "C: ProUKR~UKR","D: ProUKR~RUS",
                   "E: ProRUS~UKR","F: ProRUS~RUS")
print(data.frame(Model = model_names_6,
                 R2 = round(sapply(models_6, function(m) summary(m)$r.squared), 4)))
```

```{r hac-six-models}
hac_results_6 <- lapply(seq_along(models_6), function(i)
  coeftest(models_6[[i]], vcov = NeweyWest(models_6[[i]], lag = 4)))
for (i in seq_along(models_6)) {
  cat("\n===", model_names_6[i], "(HAC) ===\n"); print(hac_results_6[[i]])
}
```

```{r irfs-six, fig.height=5, fig.width=11}
set.seed(42)
horizon <- 6
own_g <- c("d_google_lag1","d_google_lag2")
own_u <- c("d_gt_ukraine_lag1","d_gt_ukraine_lag2")
own_r <- c("d_gt_russia_lag1","d_gt_russia_lag2")
cu    <- c("d_ukraine_lag0","d_ukraine_lag1","d_ukraine_lag2")
cr    <- c("d_russia_lag0","d_russia_lag1","d_russia_lag2")

ci_list <- list(
  bootstrap_irf_ci(mA,own_g,cu,h=horizon,n_boot=500),
  bootstrap_irf_ci(mB,own_g,cr,h=horizon,n_boot=500),
  bootstrap_irf_ci(mC,own_u,cu,h=horizon,n_boot=500),
  bootstrap_irf_ci(mD,own_u,cr,h=horizon,n_boot=500),
  bootstrap_irf_ci(mE,own_r,cu,h=horizon,n_boot=500),
  bootstrap_irf_ci(mF,own_r,cr,h=horizon,n_boot=500)
)

df_irf6 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(ci_list), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    week      = 0:(horizon-1),
    irf       = ci_list[[i]]$point,
    lower     = ci_list[[i]]$lower,
    upper     = ci_list[[i]]$upper,
    territory = ifelse(i %% 2 == 1, "Ukraine","Russia"),
    audience  = rep(c("Worldwide","Worldwide","Pro-Ukraine","Pro-Ukraine",
                      "Pro-Russia","Pro-Russia"), each = horizon)[((i-1)*horizon+1):(i*horizon)]
  )
}))

ggplot(df_irf6, aes(x = week, color = territory, fill = territory)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +

                     name = "Conflict territory") +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = c("Ukraine" = "#1A5276", "Russia" = "#C0392B"),
                    name = "Conflict territory") +
  facet_wrap(~ audience, ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "IRFs: Conflict Shock to Search Attention by Audience x Conflict Location",
       subtitle = "Shaded band = 90% bootstrap CI | Location dominates audience",
       x = "Weeks after shock", y = "SD units (search attention)") +
  theme_project()

cum <- round(sapply(ci_list, function(x) sum(x$point)), 4)
cat("Cumulative IRF effects:\n")
for (i in 1:6) cat(model_names_6[i], ":", cum[i], "\n")
```

# Extension 2 — Financial Markets and the VIX

**Cholesky ordering:** d_conflict -> r_sp500 -> d_vix

```{r vix-download}
getSymbols("VIXCLS", src = "FRED")
vix_raw      <- data.frame(date = index(VIXCLS), vix = as.numeric(VIXCLS))
vix_raw      <- vix_raw[vix_raw$date >= as.Date("2023-01-01") & !is.na(vix_raw$vix), ]
vix_raw$week <- as.Date(cut(vix_raw$date, breaks="week", start.on.monday=TRUE)) + 4
vix_weekly   <- aggregate(vix ~ week, data=vix_raw, FUN=mean)
colnames(vix_weekly) <- c("week_date","vix")
vix_weekly   <- vix_weekly[order(vix_weekly$week_date),]
vix_weekly$d_vix <- c(NA, diff(vix_weekly$vix))
cat("Weekly VIX obs:", nrow(vix_weekly), "\n")
```

```{r sp500-download}
sp500_xts <- getSymbols("^GSPC", src="yahoo",
                        from="2023-01-01", to="2026-05-01", auto.assign=FALSE)
sp500_raw      <- data.frame(date=index(sp500_xts), close=as.numeric(Cl(sp500_xts)))
sp500_raw      <- sp500_raw[!is.na(sp500_raw$close),]
sp500_raw$week <- as.Date(cut(sp500_raw$date, breaks="week", start.on.monday=TRUE)) + 4
sp500_weekly   <- aggregate(close ~ week, data=sp500_raw, FUN=tail, n=1)
colnames(sp500_weekly) <- c("week_date","sp500")
sp500_weekly$sp500   <- as.numeric(sp500_weekly$sp500)
sp500_weekly         <- sp500_weekly[order(sp500_weekly$week_date),]
sp500_weekly$r_sp500 <- c(NA, diff(log(sp500_weekly$sp500))*100)
cat("Weekly S&P 500 obs:", nrow(sp500_weekly), "\n")
```


```{r merge-vix}
df_sp500 <- df_sp500[!is.na(df_sp500$r_sp500),]
project_vix_sp <- merge(project_data_2023on, df_vix,   by="week_date", all=FALSE)
project_vix_sp <- merge(project_vix_sp,      df_sp500, by="week_date", all=FALSE)
cat("Rows after merge:", nrow(project_vix_sp), "\n")
```

```{r var-vix}
var2_data <- na.omit(project_vix_sp[, c("d_ukraine","d_russia","r_sp500","d_vix")])
lag2      <- VARselect(var2_data, lag.max=6, type="const")
p2        <- which.min(lag2$criteria["SC(n)",])
cat("BIC selects p =", p2, "\n")
est.VAR2  <- VAR(var2_data, p=p2, type="const")
Phi2 <- Acoef(est.VAR2); PHI2 <- make.PHI(Phi2)
cat("Eigenvalues:", round(abs(eigen(PHI2)$values),4), "\n")
```

```{r granger-vix}
cat("H0: d_ukraine does NOT Granger-cause r_sp500 + d_vix\n")
print(causality(est.VAR2, cause="d_ukraine")$Granger)
cat("H0: d_russia does NOT Granger-cause r_sp500 + d_vix\n")
print(causality(est.VAR2, cause="d_russia")$Granger)
cat("H0: d_vix does NOT Granger-cause conflict\n")
print(causality(est.VAR2, cause="d_vix")$Granger)

var_ukr_ctrl <- VAR(na.omit(project_vix_sp[,c("d_ukraine","r_sp500","d_vix")]),
                    p=1, type="const")
var_rus_ctrl <- VAR(na.omit(project_vix_sp[,c("d_russia","r_sp500","d_vix")]),
                    p=1, type="const")
cat("\nIndividual: d_ukraine -> d_vix (controlling S&P500)\n")
print(causality(var_ukr_ctrl, cause="d_ukraine")$Granger)
cat("\nIndividual: d_russia -> d_vix (controlling S&P500)\n")
print(causality(var_rus_ctrl, cause="d_russia")$Granger)
```

## VIX IRFs with Bootstrap Confidence Bands

The `vars` package computes bootstrap CIs natively via its `irf()` function.
Shaded bands = 95% bootstrap CI (500 replications).

```{r irfs-vix, fig.height=6, fig.width=11}
set.seed(42)

# Bootstrap IRFs from the vars package (built-in, 95% CI)
irf_ukr_vix <- irf(est.VAR2, impulse = "d_ukraine", response = "d_vix",
                   n.ahead = 19, boot = TRUE, ci = 0.95, runs = 500)
irf_rus_vix <- irf(est.VAR2, impulse = "d_russia",  response = "d_vix",
                   n.ahead = 19, boot = TRUE, ci = 0.95, runs = 500)

weeks <- 0:19

df_vix_irf <- data.frame(
  week      = rep(weeks, 2),
  irf       = c(as.numeric(irf_ukr_vix$irf$d_ukraine),
                as.numeric(irf_rus_vix$irf$d_russia)),
  lower     = c(as.numeric(irf_ukr_vix$Lower$d_ukraine),
                as.numeric(irf_rus_vix$Lower$d_russia)),
  upper     = c(as.numeric(irf_ukr_vix$Upper$d_ukraine),
                as.numeric(irf_rus_vix$Upper$d_russia)),
  territory = rep(c("Ukraine territory","Russia territory"), each = 20)
)

ggplot(df_vix_irf, aes(x = week, color = territory, fill = territory)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = irf), linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(aes(y = irf), size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Ukraine territory" = "#1E8449",
                                "Russia territory"  = "#C0392B")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = c("Ukraine territory" = "#1E8449",
                                "Russia territory"  = "#C0392B")) +
  labs(title = "Conflict Shock to VIX (Controlling for S&P 500)",
       subtitle = "Shaded band = 95% bootstrap CI (vars package, 500 reps)",
       x = "Weeks after shock", y = "Change in VIX") +
  theme_project()

cat("Cumulative VIX — Ukraine:", round(sum(irf_ukr_vix$irf$d_ukraine), 4), "\n")
cat("Cumulative VIX — Russia: ", round(sum(irf_rus_vix$irf$d_russia),  4), "\n")
```

> **Conclusion:** Normalisation holds in financial markets. Russia attacks Granger-cause
> VIX (p approx 0.016); Ukraine attacks do not (p approx 0.698). No reverse causality.
